The '''African Institute for Mathematical Sciences''' ('''AIMS''') is a pan-African network of postgraduate schools teaching mathematical sciences. Established in 2003 in Cape Town, South Africa, AIMS offers postgraduate training, research, and public engagement programs aimed at building scientific capacity across Africa. The institute was founded by physicist [[Neil Turok]] to educate African students in STEM fields to support the continent's development.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025 |title=AIMS Annual Report 2023-2024 |url=https://aims.ac.za/wp-content/uploads/sites/5/2025/07/AIMS_Annual-Report-2023-2024.pdf |website=aims.ac.za}}</ref>

== History ==

=== Founder ===
The first African Institute for Mathematical Sciences was founded in [[Muizenberg]] near Cape Town by [[Neil Turok]] in 2003, while he was Chair of Mathematical Physics at [[Cambridge University]]. Neil Turok is the son of [[Ben Turok]], an [[African National Congress|ANC]] MP. In 2008 Turok became Executive Director of the [[Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics]], and was replaced by Dr [[Robert Myers (physicist)|Robert Myers]] in 2019.

AIMS South Africa was formed as a partnership between the following universities: [[Stellenbosch University|University of Stellenbosch]], [[University of Cambridge]], [[University of Cape Town]], [[University of Oxford]], [[University of Paris-Sud]], and [[University of the Western Cape]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aims.ac.za/en/about/about-aims|title=About AIMS|publisher=AIMS South Africa|access-date=8 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170908201619/https://www.aims.ac.za/en/about/about-aims|archive-date=8 September 2017}}</ref>

=== AIMS Next Einstein Initiative ===
AIMS was the subject of a talk<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ted.com/talks/neil_turok_my_wish_find_the_next_einstein_in_africa|title=TED talk about AIMS, by Neil Turok|date=20 March 2008 |publisher=TED}}</ref> by [[Neil Turok]] after he received the [[TED Prize]] in 2008.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blog.ted.com/ted_prize_2008_1/|title=TED Prize 2008: Dave Eggers and Tutoring, Neil Turok and the next African Einstein, Karen Armstrong and the Charter for Compassion|date=28 February 2008|publisher=TED}}</ref> Neil Turok's TED wish was that, within his lifetime, an African Einstein would be celebrated.

The AIMS Next Einstein Initiative<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nexteinstein.org|title=AIMS-NextEinstein Initiative|date=21 January 2010|publisher=Nexteinstein.org}}</ref> is a plan to create 15 more AIMS centres across Africa. These centres intend to create institutions that are equipped with educational and scientific resources equivalent to the more developed continents, in order to fulfil Neil Turok's TED wish.

The first three centres created after that in South Africa are in Senegal,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aims-senegal.sn/|title=AIMS-Senegal|date=4 May 2013|publisher=Aims-senegal.sn|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110926215517/http://www.aims-senegal.sn/|archive-date=26 September 2011}}</ref> Ghana<ref name="AIMS-Ghana">{{cite web|url=http://www.aims.edu.gh//|title=AIMS-Ghana|publisher=AIMS-Ghana|access-date=11 August 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130728045124/http://www.aims.edu.gh/|archive-date=28 July 2013}}</ref> and Cameroon. AIMS Senegal became operational in September, 2011 in [[M'Bour|Mbour]], near [[Dakar]], and AIMS Ghana opened its doors in 2012 in the small coastal city of [[Biriwa]]. An earlier centre based at the [[African University of Science and Technology]] (AUST<ref>{{cite web|url=http://aust-abuja.org/|title=African University of Science and Technology|publisher=Aust-abuja.org|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111020170941/http://aust-abuja.org/|archive-date=20 October 2011}}</ref>) in Nigeria was known as AIMS [[Abuja]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://physicsworld.com/cws/article/news/34836|title=Seeking an African Einstein|publisher=Physicsworld.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tedprize.org/aims-abuja-opens/|title=AIMS Abuja Opens|publisher=Tedprize.org|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120403000731/http://www.tedprize.org/aims-abuja-opens/|archive-date=3 April 2012}}</ref> for a while. AIMS Ghana was set up in 2012, AIMS [[Cameroon]] in 2013 and AIMS [[Tanzania]] in 2014. There is a sixth centre in [[Rwanda]].

The AIMS Next Einstein Initiative is a continuation of the work of the African Mathematical Institutes Network (AMI-Net).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nepadst.org/platforms/aminet.shtml|title=African Mathematical Institutes Network|publisher=Nepadst.org}}</ref>

After AIMS [[South Africa]] won the TED Prize in 2008, Neil Turok and his partners developed the AIMS Next Einstein Initiative, the goal of which is to build 15 centres of excellence across [[Africa]] by 2023. The Government of [[Canada]] made a US$20 million investment in the Next Einstein Initiative in 2010, through its [[International Development Research Centre]], and numerous governments in Africa and Europe have followed suit. In October 2015, a forum took place in [[Dakar]] under the auspices of UNESCO's International Basic Sciences Programme to take the project for a vast network of centres to the next stage.<ref name=":13">{{Cite book|url=http://unesdoc.unesco.org/images/0023/002354/235406e.pdf|title=Southern Africa. In: UNESCO Science Report: towards 2030|last1=Kraemer-Mbula|first1=Erika|last2=Scerri|first2=Mario|publisher=UNESCO|year=2015|isbn=978-92-3-100129-1|location=Paris|pages=535–555}}</ref>

== Mission ==

=== Teaching and research ===
The AIMS institutes teach both basic and applied mathematics, covering a large range of mathematical applications in physics (including astrophysics and cosmology), quantitative biology, [[bioinformatics]], scientific computing, finance, agriculture modelling and so on. That in [[Senegal]] proposes courses in both French and English.<ref name=":13"/> In addition to its academic programmes, AIMS [[South Africa]] has a research centre in interdisciplinary areas like cosmology, computing and finance (see below). In 2015, AIMS [[Cameroon]] was planning to launch its own research centre to host resident and visiting researchers from universities in [[Cameroon]] and beyond.<ref name=":13" />

=== Community service ===
The AIMS institutes provide community services. AIMS Senegal has developed an innovative teaching module for secondary school maths teachers and has partnered with local businesses to raise funds for the creation of a national contest on computer applications and mathematical modelling, with a focus on finding development-oriented solutions. AIMS [[South Africa]] directs the AIMS Schools Enrichment Centre for primary and secondary school teachers, which also organizes public lectures, workshops and master classes and supports maths clubs in schools across the country (see below). Scholars and lecturers from AIMS Ghana have equipped teachers at [[Biriwa]] Junior High School with an innovative teaching module.<ref name=":13" />

==Locations==
AIMS lists five centres across Africa:<ref>{{Cite web |title=Our Centres |url=https://aims.ac.za/our-centres/ |website=AIMS |access-date=July 30, 2025}}</ref>
* Cameroon
* Ghana
* Rwanda 
* Senegal
* South Africa

== AIMS South Africa ==

===Academic programme===
====Structured Masters programme====
The flagship programme of AIMS [[South Africa]] is a 10-month Structured Masters programme in the Mathematical Sciences. The programme was upgraded in 2012 from a Postgraduate Diploma. The master's degree is conferred by the three South African universities in the partnership. Students from Africa can apply for full scholarships, including travel, board & lodging, tuition, and a stipend. AIMS is committed to greater participation by women in science and a geographically representative student body from the African continent.

Visiting faculty have included [[David J. C. MacKay|David MacKay]], [[Bernt Øksendal]], David Aschman ([[University of Cape Town|Cape Town]]), Alan Beardon ([[University of Cambridge|Cambridge]]), Jordi Campos ([[University of Barcelona|Barcelona]]), Jesus Cerquides ([[Spanish National Research Council]]), Patrick Dorey ([[Durham University|Durham]]), Pedro Ferreira ([[Oxford University|Oxford]]), Jan Govaerts ([[Katholieke Universiteit Leuven|Leuven]]), Barry Green ([[University of Stellenbosch|Stellenbosch]]), Gordon Johnson ([[University of Houston|Houston]]), Dirk Laurie ([[University of Stellenbosch|Stellenbosch]]), Sanjoy Mahajan ([[MIT]], [[Franklin W. Olin College of Engineering|Olin]]), [[Vincent Rivasseau]] ([[University of Paris]]), Bernd Schroers ([[Heriot-Watt University|Heriot-Watt]]), Robert de Mello Koch ([[University of the Witwatersrand|Witwatersrand]]), Rob Beezer ([[University of Puget Sound]]), Jeff Sanders ([[United Nations University International Institute for Software Technology]]), and [[Tadashi Tokieda]] ([[Stanford]]). Each visiting lecturer teaches an intensive three-week-long module.

The goal of the programme is to produce students capable of doing a high quality research-based master's degree. Special emphasis is placed on intuitive understanding, problem solving skills, collaboration, scientific writing skills, and computer modelling using [[Free Software]] such as [[SageMath]], [[SciPy]], and [[R (programming language)|R]].

AIMS offers scholarships for many alumni continuing studies in South Africa.

==== Honours Degree in Mathematical Biology ====
AIMS, in conjunction with [[Stellenbosch University|University of Stellenbosch]], offers an honours degree in [[Mathematical and theoretical biology|Mathematical Biology]] for South African students.

==== Honours Degree in Mathematical Finance ====
An honours degree in [[Mathematical finance|Mathematical Finance]] is being offered for South African students in conjunction with [[Stellenbosch University|University of Stellenbosch]] and the [[University of Cape Town]].

==== Master's and doctoral studies ====
In the [[#Research centre|AIMS Research Centre]] students, often AIMS alumni, study towards a MSc or PhD degree under supervision of a resident researcher in [[Mathematical and theoretical biology|Mathematical Biology]] and [[Mathematical finance|Mathematical Finance]].

=== Research centre ===
AIMS [[South Africa]] hosts a research centre that opened in May 2008. [[Stephen Hawking]] visited the AIMS research centre and AIMS-Next Einstein Initiative launch.<ref>{{cite news|first=Jonathan |last=Leake |url=https://www.thetimes.com/travel/destinations/africa-travel/south-africa/cape-town/stephen-hawking-in-hunt-for-africas-hidden-talent-zv8tjcn372m |title=Stephen Hawking in hunt for Africa's hidden talent |newspaper=[[The Times]]|date=11 May 2008}}</ref>

The centre specialises in [[Mathematical and theoretical biology|Mathematical Biology]], [[Applied mathematics|Industrial Mathematics]], [[Mathematical finance|Mathematical Finance]], [[Astrophysics]] & [[Physical cosmology|Cosmology]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://cosmoaims.wordpress.com/ |title=Cosmology at AIMS |publisher=Cosmoaims.wordpress.com }}</ref> and [[Computer algebra system|Computer Algebra]]. Bursaries are offered for Master's and doctoral studies.

=== School Enrichment Centre ===
AIMS South Africa hosts a School Enrichment Centre which offers free learning resources and professional development courses for South African mathematics teachers.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://aimssec.aims.ac.za |title=AIMS-SEC School Enrichment Centre |publisher=Aimssec.aims.ac.za |access-date=18 September 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110811063221/http://aimssec.aims.ac.za/ |archive-date=11 August 2011 }}</ref>

=== Workshops and conferences ===
AIMS South Africa regularly hosts short conferences or workshops in mathematics and its applications, especially in [[physics]], [[mathematical finance]], [[epidemiology]]. Other topics include [[scientific modelling]] or [[system administration]] using [[Debian|Debian GNU/Linux]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://desktop.aims.ac.za/|title=AIMS Desktop|publisher=desktop.aims.ac.za|access-date=30 October 2017|archive-date=9 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240609214906/https://desktop.aims.ac.za/}}</ref> as a platform.

=== Public lectures ===
Regular public lectures<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.aims.ac.za/en/research-centre/public-lectures |title=Public Lectures at AIMS |publisher=Aims.ac.za |access-date=7 October 2012 |archive-date=19 October 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121019150623/http://www.aims.ac.za/en/research-centre/public-lectures }}</ref> on a wide range of topics are offered by [[Eminent domain|eminent]] scientists at the forefront of research in their field.

=== Funding ===
AIMS South Africa is sponsored by international corporations, international development organisations and the South African departments of [[Department of Education (South Africa)|Education]] and [[Department of Science and Technology (South Africa)|Science and Technology]]. In February 2010, [[Google]] donated $1 million to AIMS.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://blog.ted.com/2010/02/google_donates.php|title=Google donates $1 million to AIMS|date=11 February 2010|publisher=Blog.ted.com|access-date=12 June 2010|archive-date=31 May 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100531073856/http://blog.ted.com/2010/02/google_donates.php}}</ref>

In July 2010, Canada committed CAN$20 million of federal funding to AIMS and the [[#AIMS-NEI|AIMS-Next Einstein]] Initiative.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://blog.ted.com/2010/07/canada_gives_20.php|title=Canada gives $20M to expand AIMS across Africa|date=6 July 2010|publisher=Blog.ted.com|access-date=17 July 2010|archive-date=10 July 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100710153938/http://blog.ted.com/2010/07/canada_gives_20.php}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://pm.gc.ca/eng/media.asp?id=3529 |title=PM announces Banting Postdoctoral Fellowships, support for Next Einstein Initiative |date=6 July 2010 |publisher=Pm.gc.ca |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100802163548/http://pm.gc.ca/eng/media.asp?id=3529 |archive-date=2 August 2010 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.perimeterinstitute.ca/News/In_The_Media/Perimeter_Institute_&_Canada_Partner_on_Growing_Science_&_Technology_Capacity_Globally/ Perimeter Institute & Canada Partner on Growing Science & Technology Capacity Globally]  {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100709134109/http://www.perimeterinstitute.ca/News/In_The_Media/Perimeter_Institute_%26_Canada_Partner_on_Growing_Science_%26_Technology_Capacity_Globally/ |date=9 July 2010 }}</ref> The funds are administered by the [[International Development Research Centre]] and the [[Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics]].

In September 2010, the AIMS Next Einstein Initiative [[#AIMS-NEI|AIMS-NEI]] was awarded US$2 million from [[Google]]'s Project 10^100.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.project10tothe100.com/ |title=Project 10^100 |publisher=Project10tothe100.com |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090728234553/http://www.project10tothe100.com/ |archive-date=28 July 2009 }}</ref>

Individuals donate to AIMS on GivenGain.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.givengain.com/cgi-bin/giga.cgi?cmd=donate&cause_id=2319|title=Individuals donate to AIMS on GivenGain|publisher=Givengain.com}}</ref>

== AIMS Ghana ==

AIMS Ghana is among the oldest AIMS centers.<ref name="AIMS-Ghana"/> Located in West Africa, initially based within the [[University of Ghana]] in East-Legon, then based in the idyllic village of Biriwa in the Central Region, and then moved to [[Accra]]. The center has been highly patronized by the figure of [[Francis Allotey]].<ref name="Allotey Perspective on Ghana">{{Cite news|url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-05657-5_2|title=State of Mathematics in Africa and the Way Forward. In: Analysis and Partial Differential Equations: Perspectives from Developing Countries|last=Allotey|first=Francis| publisher=Springer Cham|year=2016|isbn=978-3-030-05657-5|location=London|pages=7–13|doi=10.1007/978-3-030-05657-5_2}}</ref> After his demise, the center has been organizing summer camps to outreach recently graduated students and motivate them about math, those summer camps  are currently named as Allotey Math Summer Camp after him.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ghana.africanmathsinitiative.net/camp/|title=Allotey Math Camps|publisher=AMI|access-date=4 February 2021}}</ref> A new program to support female students in [[STEM]] has also been launched.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ug.edu.gh/news/vice-chancellor-receives-delegation-aims-ghana/|title=University of Ghana|publisher=University of Ghana|access-date=4 February 2021}}</ref>

===Academic programme===
The center has two main programs. The general course focused on mathematics and its applications, and AMMI (African Masterd of Machine Intelligence)
the course focused on Machine learning patronized by [[Google AI]]. Moustapha Cisse  is the founder and director of AMMI since 2018. The goal of AMMI is to bring the best of AI education in Africa and contribute to building a healthy ecosystem of AI practitioners committed to making a positive impact on our societies.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://aimsammi.org//|title=AIMS AMMI|publisher=AIMS Ghana|access-date=4 February 2021}}</ref>

Visiting faculty have included, for the main AIMS Master program:<ref name="AIMS-Ghana"/>
Patrick Dorey ([[Durham University]]), Barry Green ([[Stellenbosch University]]),  Bernd Schroers ([[Heriot-Watt University]]), [[Alessandro Crimi]] ([[University of Zurich]]),  Bianca Dittrich ([[Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics]]) and others.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://aimsammi.org/about-ammi///|title=AMMI Lecturers|publisher=AIMS-Ghana|access-date=4 February 2021}}</ref>  While AMMI visiting faculty included Olivier Bousquet ([[Google AI]]), Hugo Larochelle ([[Google AI]]), [[Yann LeCun]] ([[New York University]]), and others.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://aims.edu.gh/lecturers-2019-2020-msc//|title=AIMSLecturers|publisher=AIMS-Ghana|access-date=4 February 2021|archive-date=3 March 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210303091025/https://aims.edu.gh/lecturers-2019-2020-msc/}}</ref> In both programs each visiting lecturer teaches an intensive three-week-long module.

===Research===
Since 2014, AIMS Ghana started conducting research on topics related to applied mathematics and epidemiology. Among the published works, there are the projects of Dr. Olivier Menoukeu Pamen (Alexander Humboldt Chair in Ghana) about [[Stochastic]] Mortality Modelling for Dependent Coupled Lives,<ref name="Stochastic">{{cite journal|last1=Henshaw|first1=Kira|last2=Constantinescu|first2=Corina
|last3=Pamen|first3=Olivier Menoukeu|title=Stochastic Mortality Modelling for Dependent Coupled Lives|journal=Risks|volume=8|issue=1|year=2020|page=17|doi=10.3390/risks8010017|doi-access=free|hdl=10419/257972|hdl-access=free}}</ref> Dr. Alessandro Crimi about [[Epidemiology|epidemiological]] study on [[prenatal care]],<ref name="docmeup">{{cite journal|last1=Amoah|first1=Benjamin|last2=Anto|first2=Evelyn
|last3=Osei|first3=Prince|last4=Pieterson|first4=Kojo
|last5=Crimi|first5=Alessandro|title=Boosting antenatal care attendance and number of hospital deliveries among pregnant women in rural communities: a community initiative in Ghana based on mobile phones applications and portable ultrasound scans
|journal=BMC Pregnancy and Childbirth|volume=16|issue=1|year=2016|pages=1–10|doi=10.1186/s12884-016-0888-x|pmid= 27301244|pmc=4906986 |doi-access=free }}</ref> and during the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] Esther Opoku Gyasi and Prof. Francis Oduro about cost-effectiveness analysis of COVID-19 data  from Ghana.<ref name="covidghana">{{cite journal|last1=Asamoah|first1=Joshua|last2=Owusu|first2=Mark
|last3=Jin|first3=Zhen|last4=Oduro|first4=Francis
|last5=Abidemi|first5=Afeez|last6=Opoku Gyasu|first6=Esther |title=Global stability and cost-effectiveness analysis of COVID-19 considering the impact of the environment: using data from Ghana
|journal=Chaos, Solitons and Fractals|volume=140|issue=1|year=2020|article-number=110103|doi=10.1016/j.chaos.2020.110103|pmid=32834629|pmc=7351453|bibcode=2020CSF...14010103A }}</ref>
